title: What did Java 21 add overall, and why is Java 21 a common upgrade target (LTS)?

s1_definition.profdef: Java 21 is a Long-Term Support (LTS) release — supported for years (next LTS after 17). Key features: (1) VIRTUAL THREADS (JEP 444) — lightweight threads for I/O-bound concurrency, (2) PATTERN MATCHING FOR SWITCH (JEP 441) — `case Integer i -> ...` with guards, (3) RECORD PATTERNS (JEP 440) — destructure records in switch/instanceof, (4) SEQUENCED COLLECTIONS (JEP 431) — `getFirst()`, `getLast()`, `reversed()` on List/Set/Map, (5) GENERATIONAL ZGC (JEP 439) — improved low-latency GC with generational collection, (6) String Templates (preview), Unnamed Patterns (preview).
s1_definition.analogy: Java 21 is the bank's BIG renovation year (LTS = long-term building). Virtual threads = unlimited cheap clerks. Pattern matching switch = smarter case routing. Record patterns = unpack customer data inline. Sequenced collections = easy first/last access. ZGC = faster waste management.
s1_definition.oneliner: Java 21 LTS: Virtual threads, pattern matching switch, record patterns, sequenced collections, generational ZGC. LTS = long-term support = enterprise upgrade target.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Java 21 is a Long-Term Support (LTS) release — supported for years (next LTS after 17). Key features: (1) VIRTUAL THREADS (JEP 444) — lightweight threads for I/O-bound concurrency, (2) PATTERN MATCHING FOR SWITCH (JEP 441) — `case Integer i -> ...` with guards, (3) RECORD PATTERNS (JEP 440) — destructure records in switch/instanceof, (4) SEQUENCED COLLECTIONS (JEP 431) — `getFirst()`, `getLast()`, `reversed()` on List/Set/Map, (5) GENERATIONAL ZGC (JEP 439) — improved low-latency GC with generational collection, (6) String Templates (preview), Unnamed Patterns (preview).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Java 21 is the bank's BIG renovation year (LTS = long-term building). Virtual threads = unlimited cheap clerks. Pattern matching switch = smarter case routing. Record patterns = unpack customer data inline. Sequenced collections = easy first/last access. ZGC = faster waste management.

**One line to remember:** Java 21 LTS: Virtual threads, pattern matching switch, record patterns, sequenced collections, generational ZGC. LTS = long-term support = enterprise upgrade target.

sections.s2_technical:
Java 21 (LTS) is a landmark release. Virtual threads (JEP 444) become final, enabling cheap high-concurrency blocking code. Pattern matching for `switch` (JEP 441) lets a switch test types and deconstruct values: `switch (shape) { case Circle c -> ...; case Square s -> ...; }` with exhaustiveness checking against sealed types.

Record patterns (JEP 440) deconstruct records directly in `instanceof` and `switch`: `if (obj instanceof Trade(String id, BigDecimal amount))` binds `id` and `amount` in one step. Sequenced collections (JEP 431) add `getFirst()`, `getLast()`, `addFirst()`, `reversed()` to lists, deques, and linked sets. Also previewed: structured concurrency and scoped values.

A banking example: processing a sealed hierarchy of settlement instructions with a pattern-matching switch that deconstructs each record and is checked for exhaustiveness, so adding a new instruction type without handling it is a compile error. Senior nuance: Java 21 is the version most enterprises target after Java 17 because virtual threads plus pattern matching dramatically simplify concurrent, type-driven code — adopt records + sealed + switch patterns together for exhaustive, boilerplate-free domain logic.
sections.s3_banking: Problem — Dispatching on a hierarchy of settlement instructions used a chain of `instanceof` casts that was verbose and silently incomplete when a new type was added. Fix: Java 21 pattern matching for `switch` over a sealed type deconstructs each record and enforces exhaustiveness, turning a missing case into a compile error.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Input: a Buy(RELIANCE, 100) and a Sell(TCS, 50) instruction.

**Step 2.** `switch (i)` matches on the runtime type of the sealed `Instruction`.

**Step 3.** The record patterns `Buy(String s, int q)` and `Sell(String s, int q)` deconstruct each record, binding symbol and quantity directly.

**Step 4.** Because `Instruction` is sealed to just Buy and Sell, the switch is exhaustive — no default needed, and a new type would force a new case.

**Step 5.** The descriptions BUY 100 RELIANCE and SELL 50 TCS are produced.

```text
INFO: BUY 100 RELIANCE ; SELL 50 TCS
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Java 21 is an LTS release and the primary enterprise upgrade target after Java 17. The flagship feature is virtual threads (JEP 444) for scalable I/O-bound concurrency. Pattern matching for switch (JEP 441) with guards enables type-safe branching. Record patterns (JEP 440) destructure records in switch and instanceof. Sequenced collections (JEP 431) add getFirst/getLast/reversed to List, Set, and Map. Generational ZGC (JEP 439) provides sub-millisecond GC pauses. Enterprises typically upgrade LTS to LTS (8→11→17→21).
